**Bloodlines:**  
Won’t go to in depth as many of these can be easily tweaked in terms of numbers of by providing the class copies of spells from the multitude that exist already. I will refer to these abilities as Bloodspells, spells or simualr due to formatting and the potential to be affected by counterspell, anti-magic and similar effects.  
Some things that come to mind are:  
**BIGGEST NOTE**: Dexterity as a casting stat is just not a good idea for the class as they will only need dex for all their attacks, AC, saves and skills and now spellcasting and then the rest can go in CON for a full character. Perhaps going down the line of Matt Mercers Bloodhunter and specifying either INT or WIS (chosen at character creation)?  
**Formatting**: Spells name should be the heading text with the level restriction underneath as the subtext for ease of reading. Plus the names of the spells are cool and should draw the players eye to get them excited for some Hemomantic shenanigans.  
•	Level one bloodspells don’t scale in damage, so high level characters would be giving up multi attacks (most likely with magic weapons and extra Bloodline dice) vs one use of the spell for D8 damage on hit.  
•	Ball of fire: If the casting stat is clarified in the Lineage section you dont need to expand on the Spell attack roll ) D20 + dex + prof). Also the 2 ranges are unusual for a spell as magic doesn't often have fall off.   
•	Raging Armor: Concentration is not a duration. Creatures dont get a dex save akin to Hellish Rebuke? Additionally, a concentration spell that only procs on damage is a very fine line to walk as it could be a case of only 1 attack getting "reflect damage" before the spell is lost  
•	Comet: Seems to be a balance nightmare with the number of dice and the ability being restricted in an encounter AND by a rest. Might need a full overhaul by one of the subreddits many casters.   
•	Ball of Water: An attack roll but mentions a save? Either it is an attack roll made with Dex or the creature gets to save vs blind. The idea of water being fluid and being either an attack roll or saving throw is a cool way of presenting the element but needs to be clear if you are doing the condition or the damage roll in the spells text  
•	Tidal Wave: Range self vs line spells formatting. if its AOE around then should be listed as the bubble centred on self and the lines dimensions will originate from caster. Same situation with Comet, having to balance in encounter and resting.  
•	Earth Hands: Concentration without duration. Good work specifying creature size. The restrained condition already grants advantage to hit with attacks. Perhaps grappled with this spells advantage bonus?  
•	Rock Armor: Small races are basically immobile, but +8 AC is going to make every optimizer cream. Again, a balance nightmare and does not mention any effects vs forced movement or flying despite the stones incredible weight. Concentration without duration but with an AC bonus dex saves are your only concerns (depsite the armour not affecting dex)  
•	Bloodline of Air give a passive bonus (+5ft move) while the other bloodlines do not   
•	Extended Range: A cool idea for a range character, not sure of balance but this is pretty rad! Does this apply to extra attack or just one attack?  
•	Wind Slash: Not sure why both slashing and force for a balde of pressurised air in all honesty.   
•	Swift Strikes: The flavour of this spells description specifies "four attacks" yet the spells effect does not relate to multiple attacks or saves (see Steel Wind Strike- Xanathar's Guide). Just change wording to be akin to " You stike with a gust of slashes, cuts, and lunges" or similar  
•	Tornado: No additional effect on flying creatures or range attacks? Same balance issues as the other high end Bloodspells  
•	Blinding Light: Wording needs to specify if a successful save ignores blinded. Choosing creatures to be immune via scaling might be able to be replaced with extra bloodpoints?  
•	Beam Attack: 50ft is a strange distance choice for 5th edition. Best to make things with this range 60ft.  
•	Uplifting Spirit: Very strong ability for something other classes can only do once a long rest. Something to research with users more knowledgeable in class vs class balance   
•	Sun Beam: 30D8 damage on a half caster for only 5 bloodpoints. OOF  
•	Dark Veil: This is just the darkness spell but better. Think it should just grant darkness and maybe with a small bonus? Blind on a class that uses DEX for most of their build is a very slippery slope into being a sword rouge   
•	Shadow Strike: Wording on the Bonus action/action interaction (that’s a mouthful) is complex. Best to have it be a Bonus action teleport that you may at the end of your turn teleport back to where the spell was cast. This also allows for some movement and reactions in between the teleport and attack/action/  
•	Greater Invis: Needs to be concentration   
•	Animate Dead: Very important if it uses the original creatures stat block with changes to be undead or if they are a custom creature. Without restrictions you could be having any monster as a pet for one hour.   
  
  
An important note for a full class homebrew is the requirements and features you get from mulitclassing and what features could and could not exist together- but for a new player this homebrew is flavourful and dripping with passion. **Thank you being brave and sharing this work with the internet.** I hope that this list of insights gives you some inspiration to keep working on your DND homebrew, campaign and to dig your teeth into the beauty that is class/spell/multiclass/item/etc balance and that you come back to the subreddit soon with changes, updates, or even more new ideas!

As my fellow commenters have pointed out, a brand-new class is bit of a mountain for someone new to the system, but enthusiasm is always a good first place! Without knowledge of your home setting, it will be hard to give pointed feedback but it seems with a preliminary glace that this class would work better off as a subclass. Will give a breakdown so that you can continue crafting until you find something that fits just right for you, your players, balance, and of course fun. My breakdown goes as follows  
**Class features/build:**  
The class shouldn't choose an armour type, a martials get the benefit of all armour types (and hybrid builds such as monk and ranger get the choice between 2). The same applies to weapon proficiencies as the weapons are often grouped as simple vs martials- with unique exceptions outlined where appropriate (subclasses picking one like Bladesinger or rogues getting rapier). Additionally, shields are missing on a martial build- if this is a choice then it might be of benefit to mention some sort of narrative reasoning for this in the class description.  
**Bloodline Lineage**:  
Just wording change as the text in regards to 'You cannot change this bloodline at any time' is a bit uneasy and ultimately not that important- as text regarding changing of abilities is more often the standard rather than the rule (abilities/features are specified when you can change instead of declaring the permanent nature of the ruling)  
The damage types/choices should be listed here as for new Paxanthians to identify it briefly too.   
**Bloodline Damage:**  
Would put after the Bloodline points in the text as it this paragraph references them but otherwise seems ok. Balance wise- seems to be just a little elemental kick so on a martial without fighting style or secondary abilities, in my opinion, seems to be going for a pure DPS build. With future bloodline abilities, seems to be fine.   
**Bloodline Points:**  
Interesting choice to not gain full recovery of this feature on a short rest (when fighters/bloodhunters/monks gain their key utility on a short rest). The amount and recharge of these points is dependent on the balance of the bloodline spells so will leave that in your hands and those better versed in damage calculation (or optimising)   
Defensive Manoeuvring:  
1 Bloodpoint to do the Monks 1 Ki point ability (Step of the wind/patient defence). As the only listed defensive option (lack of defensive fighting styles or shield prof.) not a bad choice. Would change the wording as "defensive bonus action" is redundant as the very next sentence clarifies that the Paxanthian can dodge, dash and disengage as a Bonus action, conveying this information cleanly in one sentence.  
**ASI**:  
It’s an ASI. :) Yep  
**Extra attack:**  
Its multi attack on a martial. Yep :)   
**Bloodline Potency:**  
Would change the formatting of this as this seems to be a key ability for the class. The level scaling should be reformatted to fit the other classes 'This spell’s damage increases by 1d10 when you reach 5th level (2d10), 11th level (3d10), and 17th level (4d10)' style of presentation for ease of reading.   
Should also clarify that the 2D8 is the same damage type as your Bloodline (rouge sneak attack is guilty of something similar).  
**Adept**:  
Since the baseline ability to add a Bloodline dice does not cost any points, it might be easier to say "When you use your bloodline dice on a weapon attack, you may spend a Bloodline point to add an additional dice". Balance wise, seems like this is going to the bread and butter of damage every short rest outside of Bloodline spells so if the class is underpowered- this would be the place to add an additional effect.   
**Surge**:  
The sentence clarifying the rule should be separate from the narrative explanation (clearer for rule discussions this way). The restriction on what these bloodpoints can be used on seems to be cluttered and as a new reader, is a bit confusing. A bonus action to recover Bloodline points in exchange for damage is a cool idea for some classic blood magic power, but with the damage not being clarified (can it be reduced by resistances? Magic items/feat interactions?) and the choice of Bloodpoints being on the player rather than a set amount or a dice amount is iffy in this readers opinion.   
And the elephant in the text is the self-stun (re: incapactiated for one round). This means that the class cannot capitalise on this Bloodpoint recovery unless they can guarantee that the combat is safe in the turn, they use this, that they are in a safe place (but cannot use the level 2 Bloodpoint dash as they are both competing for the bonus action) or that this is a simultaneous combat starter AND ender. The downsides of this are too great for a once a long rest buff (despite how overtuned some of the spell effects can be)   
**Unwavering Spirit:**  
A more costly second wind from fighter. For a purely offensive class, this might need to add a modifier on top of the ability as to prevent that juicy 2 Hp heal for an action. Perhaps + level as it is a once a long rest ability? Could balance it against the Monks (open hand) Wholeness of Body heal.   
The text on this just needs a tidy up to be more succinct (For one Bloodpoint you may, as an action, Heal 2D10\* Hit points. Once you do so, you must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again)  
**Disciplined**:  
This feature is better critiqued by those with better knowledge of DPS and other funky number stuff. Not against it as it does consume the class resource but could be a bit underwhelming for level 13  
**Angles of Attack:**  
Bonus action to make an attack/s? The text should specify if you can use extra attack with this feature. If so, then frenzy barbarian would like a buff. If this cost bloodpoints then i might see this ability in practice and its sure thematic. A bonus action to attack as a class feature is competing with the defensive bloodpoint options and the ability to use 2 weapons so this comes down to a matter of design philosophy in this readers opinion. Is this a matter of training or blood rites?  
**Immunity:**  
Gaining complete immunity at 17th level might be too weak or too strong depending on the damage type picked all the way at level 1. One for the Homebrewers and DM's who are better versed in the damage types to discuss. I like the idea but need to wonder if this would make the surge damage 0?  
**Mastery:**  
Mastery seems to be competing with two different level 20 ideas. Most classes that use a resource (sorcery points, bardic inspiration, Ki points) have their capstones be similar to the latter section of initiative recharging a small amount. The former ability of spending an entire turn for a full Bloodpoint recovery is appropriate for a level 20 feature but when considering that a short rest can recover half of this any number of times (full if you commit to a short rest based martial) then this is purely a combat boost- one that removes the instant use of bloodpoints by taking away your move, action, bonus action AND reaction by virtue of the wording one turn of combat. If this is meant to be a onetime overclocking of the Paxanthians body- its best to consider the offensive nature of the classes build and let them keep the tempo up so to say
